ex.why.combo: Combinations far above or below expectation point to local demand, coverage, pricing or data-entry patterns worth checking.
ex.why.concentration: When a few values hold most records, changes in those values drive the overall picture.
ex.why.cross: Shows whether the composition of one grouping depends on the other — for example, whether profile choice differs by city.
ex.why.group_trend: Groups moving in opposite directions can be hidden inside a stable total.
ex.why.measure: Summarizes the typical value and spread of a real numeric quantity.
ex.why.measure_group: Differences between groups may reflect real differences or a different mix of records.
ex.why.pair: Related measures can help to explain each other, but a relationship is not a cause.
ex.why.small: Rarely used values can be valid niche options, discontinued options, spelling variants or test entries.
ex.why.status: A different status mix between groups can point to differences in process, coverage, timing or data entry. The data shows the pattern, not its cause.
ex.why.status_similar: Groups behave alike for this category, so differences elsewhere are not explained by it.
ex.why.trend: Volume changes over time can reflect campaigns, seasonality, capacity, outages or changes in how records are created.
ex.why.trend_change: Sudden period-to-period changes are often linked to a specific event and are worth explaining before planning on them.
ex.why.volume: Shows where volume is concentrated. A higher count is not good or bad by itself — compare it with targets, capacity or market size before judging.

findings.intro: Each card explains what the data shows, why it may matter, what you could do, and the evidence behind it.
help.quality_vs_business: A data-quality issue is a problem with how the data was recorded (duplicates, gaps, unreadable values) and should be fixed before trusting results. A business finding is a pattern in correctly recorded data that may inform a decision.
help.title: Data-quality issue or business finding?
ins.conc.action: Review the dependency on “{level}” and whether other groups can grow.

ins.conc.finding.one: Out of {count} group of “{group}”, “{level}” accounts for {share}% of total “{measure}”.
ins.conc.finding.other: Out of {count} groups of “{group}”, “{level}” accounts for {share}% of total “{measure}”.

ins.conc.limit: Totals depend on how many records each group has.
ins.conc.title: “{level}” provides {share}% of total “{measure}”
ins.conc.why: Heavy reliance on one group is a risk if it declines, and shows where results come from.
ins.diff.action: Compare what distinguishes “{high}” from “{low}” before shifting resources or targets.
ins.diff.finding: “{high}” has the highest typical “{measure}” ({high_value}); “{low}” has the lowest ({low_value}).
ins.diff.limit_median: Typical value = median, which is not affected by a few extreme records.
ins.diff.title: “{measure}” differs by “{group}”
ins.diff.why: Consistent differences between groups show where performance or behaviour diverges.
ins.dominant.action: Keep this imbalance in mind when comparing groups.
ins.dominant.title: “{value}” makes up most of “{column}”
ins.dominant.why: Comparisons involving the other values rest on fewer records.
ins.dup.action: Approve “Remove exact duplicate rows” in the Cleaning step, or confirm the copies are intentional.

ins.dup.finding.one: The same record appears more than once ({count} extra copy).
ins.dup.finding.other: The same record appears more than once ({count} extra copies).

ins.dup.why: Duplicates inflate counts and totals, so summaries may overstate activity.
ins.empty_col.action: Remove it in the Cleaning step, or check whether the export from the source system dropped it.
ins.empty_col.title: “{column}” contains no data
ins.empty_col.why: An empty column adds nothing to the analysis.
ins.impossible.action: Verify these records; approve “Set impossible values to missing” only if they are errors.
ins.impossible.title: Implausible values in “{column}”
ins.impossible.why: Implausible values usually point to entry errors and can distort totals and averages.
ins.invalid.action: Correct them at the source or approve the type conversion in the Cleaning step (originals are kept in the log).

ins.invalid.finding.one: {count} value in “{column}” are not valid {kind} (for example {examples}).
ins.invalid.finding.other: {count} values in “{column}” are not valid {kind} (for example {examples}).

ins.invalid.title: Unreadable values in “{column}”
ins.invalid.why: These values cannot be included in calculations, so totals and averages may be incomplete.
ins.keydup.action: Check with the data owner which record is correct, then remove or merge the duplicates.

ins.keydup.finding.one: {count} ID value appear on more than one record ({extra} extra records).
ins.keydup.finding.other: {count} ID values appear on more than one record ({extra} extra records).

ins.keydup.limit: Repeated IDs can be legitimate if the column is not meant to be unique.
ins.keydup.title: Some IDs in “{column}” are used more than once
ins.keydup.why: If each ID should be unique, these records may be duplicated or conflicting, which distorts totals.
ins.missing.action: Find out why values are missing and fill the gaps at the source where possible.
ins.missing.limit: Missing values are not filled in automatically.
ins.missing.title: “{column}” is {pct}% incomplete
ins.missing.why: Conclusions about this column describe only the records where it is filled in and may be biased.
ins.none.action: Collect more records or add relevant fields (such as dates, categories or measures) before drawing conclusions.
ins.none.finding: The data does not show statistically reliable trends, differences or relationships.
ins.none.reason_no_categories: There are no category columns to compare groups.
ins.none.reason_no_dates: There is no usable date column for trends.
ins.none.reason_no_measures: There are no numeric measures to compare.
ins.none.reason_weak: Measured differences and relationships are too small to be reliable.
ins.none.title: No reliable patterns found yet
ins.none.why: Acting on weak or random patterns can lead to wrong decisions.
ins.outliers.action: Check whether these are genuine (e.g. a large order) or recording errors before excluding anything.

ins.outliers.finding.one: {count} value in “{column}” are far from the rest; the largest is {max} while the typical value is {median}.
ins.outliers.finding.other: {count} values in “{column}” are far from the rest; the largest is {max} while the typical value is {median}.

ins.outliers.limit: Extreme values are not necessarily wrong.
ins.outliers.title: Unusually extreme values in “{column}”
ins.outliers.why: A few extreme values can strongly affect totals and averages.
ins.rel.action: Investigate why they move together before acting; test any change on a small scale first.
ins.rel.finding_cat: The mix of “{b}” differs noticeably between “{a}” groups ({strength} association).
ins.rel.finding_neg: Records with higher “{a}” tend to have lower “{b}” ({strength} association).
ins.rel.finding_pos: Records with higher “{a}” tend to have higher “{b}” ({strength} association).
ins.rel.why: Knowing which measures move together helps with planning and forecasting.
ins.skew.action: Report the typical (median) “{column}” rather than the average.
ins.skew.finding: Most “{column}” values are modest: the typical value is {median}, but a few large ones raise the average to {mean}.
ins.skew.title: A few large values dominate “{column}”
ins.skew.why: The average overstates what is typical.
ins.trend.action: Confirm the latest {freq} is complete, then review what changed over the period before planning.
ins.trend.finding_down: {subject} fell from {first} in {first_period} to {last} in {last_period}, with a consistent downward pattern.
ins.trend.finding_up: {subject} rose from {first} in {first_period} to {last} in {last_period}, with a consistent upward pattern.
ins.trend.limit_partial: The first and last periods may be incomplete.
ins.trend.why_negative: A sustained decline may signal a problem that needs attention.
ins.trend.why_neutral: A sustained change over time may signal a shift in activity worth understanding.
ins.trend.why_positive: If this continues, it points to growth worth sustaining.
issue.ambiguous_dates: Dates could be day-first or month-first; the format needs confirmation.
issue.constant: Column has a single distinct value ({value}).

issue.empty_rows.one: {count} row have no values at all.
issue.empty_rows.other: {count} rows have no values at all.

issue.inconsistent_labels.one: {count} group of labels differ only by case/spacing, e.g. {examples}.
issue.inconsistent_labels.other: {count} groups of labels differ only by case/spacing, e.g. {examples}.

issue.key_duplicates: Identifier '{column}' repeats: {count} value(s) appear more than once ({extra} extra row(s)) — possible duplicate records.
issue.leading_zeros: Numeric-looking codes with leading zeros; kept as text so zeros are not lost.
issue.name_inconsistent_style: Column names use mixed naming styles ({styles}).

issue.near_duplicate_rows.one: {count} row more become duplicates once whitespace and missing markers are normalized.
issue.near_duplicate_rows.other: {count} rows more become duplicates once whitespace and missing markers are normalized.

issue.outliers_extreme.one: {count} outlier far outside the typical range (outside {low} – {high}); verify before excluding.
issue.outliers_extreme.other: {count} outliers far outside the typical range (outside {low} – {high}); verify before excluding.

issue.outliers_mild.one: {count} value outside the typical range; may be legitimate.
issue.outliers_mild.other: {count} values outside the typical range; may be legitimate.

issue.skewed: Distribution is strongly skewed (skew {skew}); prefer the median ({median}) to the mean.

issue.small_sample.one: Only {count} row; statistics and tests have limited reliability.
issue.small_sample.other: Only {count} rows; statistics and tests have limited reliability.

kpi.records_sub.one: of {count} record in the original file
kpi.records_sub.other: of {count} records in the original file

lim.causation: Correlations and group differences describe associations in this data only; they do not show causation.
lim.causation_short: This is an association, not proof that one causes the other.
lim.high_missing: High missingness (≥20%) in {columns}; results for these columns use available values only and may be biased.

lim.multiple_tests.one: {count} statistical test were run; results are adjusted (Benjamini–Hochberg) to limit false discoveries.
lim.multiple_tests.other: {count} statistical tests were run; results are adjusted (Benjamini–Hochberg) to limit false discoveries.

lim.partial_periods: Trend periods at the start and end of the date range may be incomplete.
lim.provisional: Type conversion is still pending review for {columns}; these columns were analyzed with provisional reading. Approve or reject the conversions in the Cleaning step.

lim.small_sample.one: Only {count} row: estimates are unstable and tests have little power.
lim.small_sample.other: Only {count} rows: estimates are unstable and tests have little power.

lim.sparse_tables: Some category comparisons rely on small groups.

loading.engine: Preparing the analysis engine in your browser… (first visit only, about a minute)

note.first_sheet_only.one: The workbook has {count} sheet; only the first sheet '{sheet}' was loaded.
note.first_sheet_only.other: The workbook has {count} sheets; only the first sheet '{sheet}' was loaded.

note.partial_periods: The first and last periods may be partial, which can distort the ends of the series.

note.trailing_blank_lines.one: {count} blank line at the end of the file were ignored.
note.trailing_blank_lines.other: {count} blank lines at the end of the file were ignored.

op.key_duplicates_kept: Rows with duplicate identifiers kept (not approved).
op.no_mode: No values to compute a mode.
op.not_converted: Column was not converted to a number/date, so plausibility rules were not applied.
op.not_numeric: Column is not numeric (type conversion not applied).

quality.no_key_dups: No repeated values in identifier-like columns.

sum.desc.domain: It appears to describe {domain}, based on columns such as {columns}.
sum.desc.identifiers: Identifier and code columns ({columns}) are never averaged or correlated; they are used for duplicate checks and, in Analyze, as groupings.
sum.desc.no_dates: No date column was found, so changes over time cannot be assessed.

sum.desc.records.one: This dataset contains {count} record with {columns} columns.
sum.desc.records.other: This dataset contains {count} records with {columns} columns.

sum.evidence.good.one: {count} reliable finding supported by the data.
sum.evidence.good.other: {count} reliable findings supported by the data.

sum.evidence.insufficient.one: The data does not contain enough evidence for firm conclusions ({count} record analyzed).
sum.evidence.insufficient.other: The data does not contain enough evidence for firm conclusions ({count} records analyzed).

sum.evidence.limited.one: Findings are based on only {count} record; treat them as indicative.
sum.evidence.limited.other: Findings are based on only {count} records; treat them as indicative.

sum.evidence.quality: Urgent data-quality problems remain; resolve them before relying on the findings.
sum.none: Nothing to report in this section.
sum.none_findings: No reliable findings yet — see the evidence note above.
sum.none_opportunities: The data does not point to specific opportunities.
sum.none_risks: No risks or unusual changes were detected.
